title: AIWatcher Enterprise - Lifecycle Requirements and Scenario Test Suite
summary: Enterprise coverage for AIWatcher as an organizational control loop across local developer agents and production AI applications.

scope.position: AIWatcher Enterprise is the organizational control loop for AI work. It unifies local developer agents and SDK-instrumented production AI applications, then lets teams apply cost, security, usage, billing-allocation, and approval controls with evidence.
scope.enterprise_boundary: Enterprise monetizes coordination, enforcement, accountability, and evidence: shared visibility, policy controls, customer and feature attribution, billing/allocation evidence for AI usage, runtime SDK enforcement, HITL, SSO/RBAC, retention, SIEM/FinOps integrations, and compliance exports.
scope.oss_dependency: AIWatcher Local is the trusted distribution wedge and individual control loop. Enterprise should propagate shared lifecycle language, evidence vocabulary, outcome model, local/app telemetry normalization, and privacy posture, while adapting personal controls into team-managed policies.
strategic_filter: Prevent customer, team, or org-level cost and security problems before damage happens.
Connect AI activity to useful outcomes at customer, feature, project, team, and business levels.
Apply a control, not just display a chart.
Prove what policy fired, what happened afterward, and what value was protected.
Strengthen the OSS-to-Enterprise upgrade path without weakening OSS developer trust.
not_scope: A generic trace viewer or LLM observability dashboard.
A collection-only product with no runtime controls.
Silent prompt/source collection from developer machines.
Enterprise claims that local/desktop platforms are intercepted without verified host lifecycle support.
Customer billing enforcement without explicit customer, plan, feature, entitlement, allowance, and billing-period metadata.
Invoices, payment collection, taxes, refunds, revenue recognition, or contract management as the system of record.

acceptance_rules.title: Control before dashboard
acceptance_rules.body: Every enterprise finding should have a next action: observe, alert, route, throttle, block, redact, require approval, export evidence, or create a policy.

acceptance_rules.title: Evidence after every intervention
acceptance_rules.body: Every policy evaluation, routing decision, block, approval, and override must produce evidence with rule version, matched telemetry, decision, actor, and measured or estimated impact.

acceptance_rules.title: Local trust boundary remains visible
acceptance_rules.body: Prompts and source remain local by default. Enterprise receives normalized metadata and evidence by default; content collection requires explicit configuration and cannot silently expand.

acceptance_rules.title: Observe-only before enforcement
acceptance_rules.body: Enterprise policies should support dry-run and observe-only modes before hard blocking, so teams can measure false positives and expected business impact.

acceptance_rules.title: Outcome beats token volume
acceptance_rules.body: Enterprise cost reporting must move toward cost per customer, feature, useful outcome, accepted output, or surviving change, not only spend and token totals.

acceptance_rules.title: Billing evidence, not billing platform
acceptance_rules.body: AIWatcher may help resolve customer AI billing and credit conflicts by proving entitlement, allowance, policy decision, enforcement acknowledgement, execution, allocation, and outcome. It must integrate with billing systems rather than replace invoices, payments, refunds, taxes, revenue recognition, or contracts.

examples.situation: A free-trial customer repeatedly triggers an expensive sequence generation feature.
examples.response: Usage Rule flags plan mismatch, routes future calls to a cheaper model or blocks after quota, and records protected spend evidence.

examples.situation: A developer's Claude Code session enters a long retry loop on a payment service.
examples.response: Local telemetry appears in the enterprise Inbox with loop pressure, cost velocity, and a recommended stop/rescope action.
examples.buyer_value: Turns local agent visibility into team-level operational control.

examples.situation: An AI feature starts using Opus for low-complexity customer requests.
examples.response: Model routing policy detects misuse, simulates savings, and applies Sonnet/Haiku routing with evidence.
examples.buyer_value: Reduces cost while maintaining product behavior.

examples.situation: A production agent attempts a sensitive data export after prompt-injection-like instructions.
examples.response: Security policy blocks or routes to HITL, records chain evidence, and exports an audit package.
examples.buyer_value: Prevents risky action and creates compliance evidence.

examples.situation: The CFO asks why AI spend grew 40 percent this month.
examples.response: Reports show spend by customer, feature, model, local team, policy decision, and outcome, with top controllable causes.
examples.buyer_value: Moves AI spend from unexplained line item to managed budget.

examples.situation: A customer disputes AI credit consumption for an expensive workflow.
examples.response: AIWatcher shows the billing period, plan allowance, customer/user/workflow allocation, policy decision, enforcement acknowledgement, actual model call, observed cost, and accepted or failed outcome.
examples.buyer_value: Support, finance, and product can resolve the conflict with evidence without changing the billing system of record.

open_decisions.options: Evaluate controls only in hosted API first, or ship a shared policy evaluator that can also run in SDK/local collector contexts.
open_decisions.recommendation: Start hosted for Enterprise Usage Rules, but design a portable rule schema so SDK/local enforcement can share semantics.

open_decisions.options: Manual plan metadata in SDK events first, or Stripe/Chargebee/custom billing sync from day one.
open_decisions.recommendation: Start with explicit SDK metadata and CSV/API import; add billing integrations after rule value is proven.

open_decisions.options: Reuse the OSS generator from aiwatcher-local, duplicate a private generator in this docs repo, or keep generated Markdown manual for now.
open_decisions.recommendation: Reuse the OSS generator pattern, but keep enterprise source and generated pages private. Avoid public enterprise roadmap leakage.

open_decisions.options: Let org admins centrally enforce local prompt/tool controls, or keep local gates developer-controlled with org-visible evidence only.
open_decisions.recommendation: Default to developer-controlled local gates plus org-visible metadata. Add centrally enforced local controls only with explicit enterprise admin and developer disclosure.

requirements.user_value: One view of every AI tool, product agent, model, app, project, feature, customer, and owner.
A morning action list for cost, risk, approvals, evidence gaps, runaway sessions, and policy drift.
Every proposed action is evaluated against its WorkUnit context (customer, plan, feature, workflow) before it executes.
Prevent customers, features, users, or agents from exceeding plan limits or destroying margin.
Route to cheaper models, throttle, block, or require approval when usage crosses thresholds.
Route high-impact actions to humans with decision evidence and expiry.
Show cost per useful business result, accepted output, customer, feature, and surviving change.

requirements.requirement: AI usage billing and allocation evidence
requirements.user_value: Resolve customer, plan, team, feature, or workflow billing conflicts by linking allowance context to policy, enforcement, execution, cost, and outcome evidence.
Export what happened, what policy applied, who approved, and whether the chain verifies.
OSS improvements strengthen Enterprise without copying personal-only behavior blindly.
SSO/RBAC, SIEM, FinOps, billing, and dashboard integrations work without weakening developer trust.

A policy decision (allow/route/throttle/block/approval) is only treated as enforced once the SDK confirms the alternative action was actually applied -- decision and enforcement are never collapsed into one fact.

workflows.title: Monday control review
workflows.body: VP Engineering opens Inbox and sees customer overage risk, runaway local sessions, HITL approvals, evidence gaps, model misuse, and top policy opportunities.

workflows.title: Usage rule dry run
workflows.body: Platform leader creates a Customer Monthly AI Budget rule, runs it against the last 30 days, and sees affected customers, protected spend, false-positive candidates, and recommended action.

workflows.title: Runtime enforcement
workflows.body: SDK calls evaluateControl before expensive model/tool calls; AIWatcher returns allow, route, throttle, block, or approval required, then records evidence.

workflows.title: Evidence export
workflows.body: Security or finance exports a session/policy evidence package with chain verification, decision timeline, approvals, risk reasons, and cost impact.

workflows.title: Billing conflict resolution
workflows.body: Support, finance, or product opens a customer usage dispute and sees billing-period allowance, allocation by user/team/feature/workflow, policy decision, enforcement acknowledgement, actual execution, observed outcome, confidence, and exportable receipt. The workflow explains AI usage; it does not issue invoices, refunds, or credits directly.

workflows.title: OSS parity review
workflows.body: Each OSS scenario is classified as propagate, adapt, OSS-only, or enterprise-only so the two products compound instead of drifting.

platforms.mechanism: Next.js dashboard, APIs, org auth, and Postgres-backed evidence/control model
platforms.coverage: Inbox, Controls, Work Ledger, Evidence, Reports, Settings target navigation
platforms.verify: Confirm current routes map to the lifecycle and remove/merge redundant dashboards.

platforms.mechanism: track, trackLLM, trackStream, session APIs, metadata, and future evaluateControl
platforms.coverage: Production app telemetry today; runtime controls pending
platforms.verify: Add customerId, planId, feature, entitlement context, and pre-call control evaluation.

platforms.mechanism: App instrumentation package for backend agents and AI workflows
platforms.coverage: Telemetry/evidence foundation; parity with JS control API pending
platforms.verify: Align event fields and policy evaluation with JS SDK.

platforms.mechanism: Zero-code local scanner and developer control loop
platforms.coverage: Local work visibility; enterprise sync/parity pending
platforms.verify: Decide which OSS events/evidence sync to Enterprise and how developer consent/admin disclosure works.

platforms.mechanism: SDK metadata first; later Stripe, Chargebee, or custom billing import
platforms.coverage: Required for customer entitlement rules and billing/allocation evidence; AIWatcher is not the billing system of record
platforms.verify: Define plan, quota, allowance, contract, billing-cycle, credit, refund, and invoice identifiers without taking ownership of invoicing or payment state.

platforms.mechanism: Evidence exports and future webhook/SIEM sink
platforms.coverage: Audit evidence target, not primary workflow yet
platforms.verify: Define minimal export and alert payloads for security teams.

platforms.coverage: Cost reporting exists in pieces; protected spend and rule effectiveness pending
platforms.verify: Connect cost reports to controls, not only charts.

scenarios.title: Unified agent inventory across local and production
scenarios.go: Open Enterprise Work Ledger or Agents.
scenarios.do: Review local Claude/Codex/Cursor agents beside SDK-instrumented product agents.
scenarios.expected: Agents are grouped by source, owner, app, project, environment, model, and last activity.
scenarios.value: Shows the differentiated local + production platform story.
scenarios.why: This is the cross-surface visibility moat competitors lack.

scenarios.title: Cost attribution by app, customer, feature, project, and model
scenarios.do: Filter by local/app surface, customer, feature, project, agent, and model.
scenarios.expected: Spend is attributed to business owners and product surfaces, not only raw token totals.
scenarios.value: Answers finance and product margin questions.
scenarios.why: Customer/feature attribution is the bridge from observability to business control.

scenarios.title: Customer entitlement context is visible
scenarios.go: Open a customer or product-feature drilldown.
scenarios.do: Inspect plan, quota, contract, billing cycle, usage, and AI cost.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher shows whether customer usage is within plan, nearing limit, or margin-negative.
scenarios.value: Foundation for Danny's Usage Rules idea.
scenarios.why: Without entitlement context, usage rules become generic budget alerts.

scenarios.title: Morning Inbox prioritizes action
scenarios.do: Review runaway cost, risky actions, HITL pending, evidence gaps, policy drift, and customer overage risk.
scenarios.expected: Inbox ranks items by controllability and business impact with clear next actions.
scenarios.value: Creates the daily enterprise habit.
scenarios.why: The product must be an action surface, not a dashboard maze.

scenarios.title: Inbox links local session issues to team ownership
scenarios.go: Open a local runaway or high-risk coding session item.
scenarios.do: Inspect owner, repo/project, team, cost velocity, evidence, and recommended policy.
scenarios.expected: Manager can act without seeing prompt/source content by default.
scenarios.value: Preserves developer trust while enabling org accountability.
scenarios.why: This is how OSS Local upgrades into Enterprise without feeling hostile.

scenarios.title: Policy templates map to lifecycle problems
scenarios.do: Create a policy from templates: cost cap, model routing, customer quota, security approval, loop breaker.
scenarios.expected: Templates explain what they prevent, what evidence they create, and whether they run observe-only or enforced.
scenarios.value: Makes control adoption easy for design partners.
scenarios.why: Enterprise buyers need fast, safe configuration.

scenarios.title: Policy simulator previews last 30 days impact
scenarios.do: Run dry-run simulation over recent events.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher shows affected sessions/customers, estimated protected spend, false-positive candidates, and sample evidence.
scenarios.value: Reduces fear of enforcement.
scenarios.why: Observe-only and simulation are enterprise adoption unlocks.

scenarios.title: SDK metadata completeness check
scenarios.do: Inspect whether app events include customerId, feature, model, planId, and outcome metadata.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher flags missing fields required for customer usage rules and margin reports.
scenarios.value: Prevents weak integrations before leadership reviews data.
scenarios.why: Enterprise controls are only as good as attribution metadata.

scenarios.title: Pre-call control evaluation
scenarios.go: Instrument a product AI call with SDK evaluateControl, declaring the WorkUnit context (customer, plan, feature, workflow) that the proposed action belongs to.
scenarios.do: Make an expensive request near customer quota.
scenarios.expected: Hosted policy engine evaluates the proposed action against its WorkUnit context and returns allow, route, throttle, block, or approval before the AI call executes.
scenarios.value: Prevents cost/security problems before the model call.
scenarios.why: This is the shift from observability to runtime control, evaluated against the canonical WorkUnit -- the business task being completed -- rather than a bare API call.

scenarios.title: Policy decision does not break customer app
scenarios.go: Run SDK with AIWatcher unavailable or policy API slow.
scenarios.do: Trigger a tracked AI call.
scenarios.expected: SDK follows configured fail-open/fail-closed mode and records local diagnostic metadata.
scenarios.value: Production apps can adopt controls safely.
scenarios.why: Enterprise runtime controls must be reliable and explicit about failure mode.

scenarios.title: Security policy can block or require approval
scenarios.go: Configure policy for sensitive data export or destructive tool use.
scenarios.do: Trigger matching agent action.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher blocks or creates HITL request with risk reasons and evidence.
scenarios.value: Security control with proof.
scenarios.why: Security and cost controls share the same policy/evidence infrastructure.

scenarios.title: Customer monthly AI budget rule
scenarios.do: Create rule: customer monthly AI cost must stay below plan allowance.
scenarios.expected: Rule can run observe-only, alert, throttle, route, block, or require approval.
scenarios.value: Prevents customers from using more AI than they pay for.
scenarios.why: This is Danny's core enterprise value prop.

scenarios.title: Premium model entitlement rule
scenarios.go: Create rule for Opus/GPT premium model access by plan.
scenarios.do: A non-entitled customer triggers a premium model request.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher routes to allowed model or blocks with evidence.
scenarios.value: Protects gross margin and plan packaging.
scenarios.why: Model routing is more valuable when tied to customer entitlement.

scenarios.title: Free trial abuse guard
scenarios.go: Create free-trial quota and velocity rule.
scenarios.do: Trial user triggers high-volume AI calls.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher throttles, blocks, or routes cheaper based on configured action.
scenarios.value: Stops unprofitable abuse without custom engineering.
scenarios.why: Common pain for AI-native SaaS companies.

scenarios.title: Feature-level margin guardrail
scenarios.go: Create rule for a product feature budget or cost per successful result.
scenarios.do: Feature cost spikes above margin threshold.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher alerts, routes, throttles, or blocks based on feature economics.
scenarios.value: Protects product margin at feature level.
scenarios.why: Feature-level AI margin is a stronger buyer metric than token cost.

scenarios.title: Model misuse recommendation becomes policy
scenarios.go: Open cost finding for expensive model misuse.
scenarios.do: Apply recommended route from premium model to cheaper model for low-complexity work.
scenarios.expected: Recommendation becomes a controlled policy with evidence and impact tracking.
scenarios.value: Closes the loop from finding to control.
scenarios.why: Dashboards end at insight; AIWatcher should apply control.

scenarios.title: Runaway production session breaker
scenarios.go: Configure max cost, retries, or events per session.
scenarios.do: Production agent enters retry loop.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher stops, pauses, or requires approval with evidence.
scenarios.value: Stops runaway costs while work is happening.
scenarios.why: Same control logic as OSS loop detection, adapted to production.

scenarios.title: Approval inbox with evidence and expiry
scenarios.do: Approver reviews context and approves/denies.
scenarios.expected: Decision records approver, expiry, risk reasons, action summary, and linked event.
scenarios.value: Enterprise accountability for high-impact AI actions.
scenarios.why: HITL is a premium control primitive.

scenarios.title: Session audit chain verification
scenarios.do: Verify chain and inspect policy decisions.
scenarios.expected: Chain status, events, risks, approvals, cost, and policy evidence are exported.
scenarios.value: Security/compliance can trust the record.
scenarios.why: Tamper-evident evidence differentiates from normal dashboards.

scenarios.title: Usage rule evidence receipt
scenarios.do: Inspect matched telemetry, customer plan context, decision, action, and impact.
scenarios.expected: Receipt proves what would have happened, what happened instead, and why.
scenarios.value: Makes preventive controls credible to finance and customer teams.
scenarios.why: Protected spend needs evidence, not vibes.

scenarios.title: Cost per customer outcome
scenarios.do: Filter by customer and product feature.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher shows AI cost per successful business outcome or accepted output where metadata exists.
scenarios.value: Connects AI spend to revenue and margin.
scenarios.why: Outcome-aware cost is the enterprise version of OSS cost per useful change.

scenarios.title: Protected spend report
scenarios.do: Review policy decisions over a period.
scenarios.expected: Report shows spend protected by routing, throttling, blocking, caching, and approvals.
scenarios.value: Turns controls into ROI.
scenarios.why: This is the CFO/VP Eng proof loop.

scenarios.title: Local surviving change signal rolls up to enterprise
scenarios.go: Review local coding work for a team.
scenarios.do: Inspect useful/rework/abandoned outcomes and surviving change evidence.
scenarios.expected: Enterprise shows team-level outcome economics without exposing prompt/source content by default.
scenarios.value: Connects developer AI work to useful engineering output.
scenarios.why: This adapts OSS outcome moat into team value.

scenarios.title: OSS scenario propagation matrix is maintained
scenarios.do: Review each OSS scenario decision: propagate, adapt, OSS-only, enterprise-only.
scenarios.expected: Every OSS feature has an enterprise disposition and target scenario.
scenarios.value: Keeps product lines aligned.
scenarios.why: Prevents drift between OSS and Enterprise.

scenarios.title: Policy recommendation learns from outcomes
scenarios.do: Review why a rule/model route/approval threshold is suggested.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher cites workload pattern, past outcomes, policy history, and measured impact.
scenarios.value: Builds the intervention graph moat.
scenarios.why: The hard-to-copy asset is which controls work for which agentic workload patterns.

scenarios.title: Weekly executive improvement summary
scenarios.do: Review top controls applied, spend protected, risks reduced, outcomes improved, and remaining gaps.
scenarios.expected: Report is board/leadership-ready and links to evidence.
scenarios.value: Creates enterprise habit and renewal evidence.
scenarios.why: Enterprise needs recurring proof that AIWatcher changed behavior.

scenarios.title: SSO/RBAC separates developer and admin control
scenarios.do: Configure roles for viewer, approver, policy admin, and org admin.
scenarios.expected: Users can see appropriate data and actions without silent expansion of local collection.
scenarios.value: Enterprise trust and procurement requirement.
scenarios.why: Control without RBAC is not enterprise-ready.

scenarios.title: SIEM/FinOps/billing export path
scenarios.do: Configure evidence, spend, and policy-impact exports.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher exports normalized records without prompt/source content by default.
scenarios.value: Fits existing enterprise workflows.
scenarios.why: Enterprises need AIWatcher to feed systems they already trust.

scenarios.title: Enforcement acknowledgement is a distinct, recorded checkpoint
scenarios.go: After evaluateControl returns a decision (route, throttle, block, or approval), call the SDK's enforcement acknowledgement step once the alternative action is actually applied.
scenarios.do: Simulate the SDK applying the routed/blocked alternative and confirming that application back to AIWatcher.
scenarios.expected: AIWatcher records enforcement acknowledgement as an event separate from the policy decision and from execution; a decision alone (for example a returned `block`) is never treated as proof the action was blocked.
scenarios.value: Prevents false confidence from policy responses that were never actually enforced; evidence proves invocation, not just intent.
scenarios.why: Strategy principle 'Prove invocation; never infer enforcement': Policy evaluated, Enforcement requested, Enforcement acknowledged, Action executed, and Action prevented must not be collapsed into one event.

scenarios.title: Customer AI billing conflict has an evidence receipt
scenarios.go: Open an Inbox item for a customer disputing AI credit or overage consumption.
scenarios.do: Inspect the receipt for the disputed billing period and workflow.
scenarios.expected: Receipt shows customer, plan, entitlement, allowance, billing period, user/team/feature/workflow allocation, proposed model/action, policy evaluation, decision, enforcement acknowledgement, actual execution, observed cost, outcome, confidence, and integration source. Missing allowance, invoice, credit, or outcome fields are labeled insufficient data rather than guessed.
scenarios.value: Support, finance, product, and platform teams can resolve AI usage disputes with shared evidence while the billing platform remains the system of record.
scenarios.why: Customer discovery suggests billing conflict may be a sharper enterprise pain than attribution alone, but AIWatcher should win it through control and evidence, not by becoming billing software.
